problem: "Short digests are one reason MD5 and SHA-1 failed" is misleading. MD5 and SHA-1 were broken by cryptanalytic attacks on their compression functions that produced collisions far below the birthday bound; digest length was not the cause of the break, it only leaves a thin margin today.
fix: MD5 and SHA-1 failed because cryptanalysts broke their compression functions and found collisions far below the birthday bound (well under 2^64 and 2^80 respectively). Their short digests also leave a thin margin today: 64 bits for MD5 and 80 bits for SHA-1.

problem: "Second preimage resistance implies preimage resistance" is stated as a general fact, but it does not hold for every hash function; it is true only for random-oracle-like functions. Some textbooks add this caveat, so a sharp student may be confused when they meet it.
fix: Say: "Collision resistance implies second preimage resistance for any hash function. Second preimage resistance implies preimage resistance for functions that behave like a random oracle, which is the case assumed for real hashes."

problem: Keeping salt plus H(salt ‖ password) with a fast hash such as SHA-256 is exactly the practice password crackers exploit; the bullet reads like a recommendation. The Beyond note mentions Argon2, but the use-list itself should not suggest plain salted SHA-256.
fix: Password storage: keep a random salt and a deliberately slow, memory-hard hash of salt ‖ password (PBKDF2, bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2), never the password itself. Salting defeats precomputed tables; slowness defeats guessing.

where: Section 4, hash tables and deduplication bullet
problem: A cryptographic digest is a poor bucket index. In-memory hash tables use cheap non-cryptographic hashes because speed matters and attackers are not the concern; mixing the two in one bullet can mislead.
fix: Split it: "Hash tables use a fast non-cryptographic hash as the bucket index. Content-addressed storage and deduplication use a cryptographic digest as the file name, so identical files map to the same name."
